correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern chosen opening and canyon descent
correspondence.finding: The chosen northwestern opening and first southeastward descent occupy the Copper Canyon and Last Chance Canyon landform setting. The source relief and labelled canyons orient the beginning, but do not supply a stream hydronym for the whole upper selection. Cottonwood Creek is a separately mapped northeastern approach. Canyon names are not promoted to verified river names.

correspondence.component_scope: Western alluvial-fan approach and connection to Death Valley Wash
correspondence.finding: After the canyon outlet, the selected route proceeds south across the western valley-floor and fan setting before reaching the mapped Death Valley Wash corridor. The detailed source separately depicts Cottonwood Creek and Oriental Wash joining the northern wash farther east. It does not establish the full selected western through-route or its joining passage into that wash. Those nearby names and shared valley membership cannot substitute for the missing selected connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Death Valley Wash and Grapevine receiving reach
correspondence.finding: The selected middle route corresponds at ordinary corridor scale to the repeatedly labelled Death Valley Wash, including the crossing near Ubehebe Crater Road, the separately labelled Little Grapevine Creek approach from the northeast, and the southeastward valley between the western mountains and the Grapevine Range. This establishes the local wash name and receiving setting; the selection contains no separate tributary fragment tracing Little Grapevine Creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Death Valley Wash to Mesquite Flat and Salt Creek transfer
correspondence.finding: South of the mapped Death Valley Wash, the selection continues over a long valley-floor interval through the Mesquite Flat setting and toward the Highway 190 crossing near Devils Cornfield. The detailed map shows the northern wash, the intervening flat and dunes, and a separate Salt Creek channel farther southeast, but does not establish the entire chosen through-link between them. Dune or valley-floor relief and the model line alone are insufficient connection evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Salt Creek corridor and Cottonball Basin entry
correspondence.finding: From the Highway 190 crossing onward, the selected southeastward route corresponds at ordinary scale to the repeatedly labelled Salt Creek channel and its approach to Cottonball Basin. The creek is mapped distinctly from the unestablished Mesquite Flat transfer. The NPS management plan independently recognizes Salt Creek as a park stream; that regional prose does not join it to the entire northern wash selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Cottonball Basin and southern Salt Creek passage
correspondence.finding: The source depicts Salt Creek entering the eastern Cottonball Basin setting and continuing south along the narrow eastern salt-flat corridor west of Furnace Creek. The selected nearly north-south segment occupies that same generalized passage. Cottonball Marsh is separately labelled along the western basin margin, and its wetland label is not assigned to the selected eastern channel. No exact modern bank, seasonal wetted extent, or continuous-flow assertion is required or made.

correspondence.component_scope: Furnace Creek Wash receiving setting and actual Middle Basin terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected final southward reach passes the separately mapped Furnace Creek Wash receiving setting and ends within the mapped Middle Basin salt-flat setting on the Salt Creek corridor. The map depicts the surrounding creek and playa passage beyond this modeled endpoint; therefore the selected endpoint is not asserted to be the natural creek mouth, the southernmost Death Valley outlet, or an open-sea terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and upper northeast-trending Palmar
correspondence.finding: Casler Figures 1–2 name the western mountain branch Río Palmar; its northeast ascent in map view and northern bend correspond to the selected opening and upper course. The separately mapped Río Lajas lies to the south and is not the chosen opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern bend, Lajas join and El Diluvio/Tres Ríos passage
correspondence.finding: Casler maps the Palmar–Lajas junction and El Diluvio dam site, with the Palmar continuing southeast. Rincón’s 2017 prose and Figure 2d identify the resulting El Diluvio/Tres Ríos reservoir and its Palmar, Lajas and Caño Pescado inputs. Together these establish the selected through-corridor without requiring a modern reservoir shoreline or operating record.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle southeast-trending river and intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: Casler maps a continuous named Palmar below El Diluvio, passing the road-crossing and Villa del Rosario setting and receiving the separately identified La Ge tributary. The selected bends and uninterrupted downstream corridor agree with this map and the regional hydrography.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower plain and eastward reach
correspondence.finding: The source maps continue the named Palmar eastward across the western lake plain, including the intervening mapped reaches and joins. Rincón describes the middle and lower agricultural corridor; no different named mainstem is introduced along the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeast lake approach and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: Both Casler study maps and the Zulia hydrography carry the lower Palmar to the west shore of Lago de Maracaibo. Casler’s mouth station and prose corroborate the terminal. The selected ending is the Palmar lake mouth, not an open-sea outlet or the Los Olivitos wetland system.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern selected opening and southwestward feeder
correspondence.finding: The eastern opening lies on an unnamed natural-watercourse line that continues slightly beyond the selected starting position. The selected southwestward feeder passes a separate approach from the east and joins a longer northern approach before continuing southwest. The chosen opening is geographically supported, without identifying it as the natural source or assigning either neighboring branch name.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern descent and Chimborazo junction
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues southwest, then south and west through the mapped joining network. The source explicitly labels Q. Chimborazo on the separate southeastern approach at the southern turn. The selected headward branch approaches from the northeast and does not ascend that labeled southeastern branch; the label is not extended to the complete selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern westward bend and northwestern receiving course
correspondence.finding: The selected southern bend follows the connected receiving drainage westward and then northwest. Separate channels enter from the south and northeast. Several short modeled bends simplify the source channel, but the approach, southern turn and northwestern continuation are accounted for at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle converging channel strands
correspondence.finding: The selected line follows the common west-northwest receiving corridor where southern and northern channel strands converge. It locally lies between the individually drawn strands and crosses from the vicinity of one to the other before their mapped convergence. The source supplies the connected converging-channel setting; this is generalized corridor correspondence rather than evidence for a separate natural channel along every modeled segment. No exact channel thread, bank or present inter-strand surface flow is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward turn and approach to the salar
correspondence.finding: The selected route turns north, passes a separate eastern joining drainage, then continues northwest along the mapped southern approach to the compact salt-flat surface. Nearby eastern parallel approaches remain distinct. The channel-line ending at the salt-flat margin is explained by the separately mapped salar footprint rather than treated as an unviewed land interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Salar Mar Muerto passage and northern departure
correspondence.finding: The selected route enters the southern end of the compact mapped surface, crosses its interior northward and leaves beside the northern channel junction. The IGM polygon attributes explicitly name Salar Mar Muerto and classify it as Salar. The natural-watercourse and surface originals together show the southern and northern channel endings meeting the corresponding margins. Geographic passage is therefore accounted for at ordinary scale. No permanent lake, continuous river channel across salt crust, overflow regime or operating managed connection is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern branch and Profeta junction
correspondence.finding: North of the salar, the selected course follows the mapped west-northwest channel while a separate northeastern branch enters the same junction setting. Farther west the watercourse labeled Q. del Profeta approaches from the south and joins the selected receiving course. The selected route does not ascend that southern Profeta branch, and its hydronym is not imposed on the unnamed western course or the salar crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: Western selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selection follows the mapped westward natural-watercourse corridor and ends on that line, inland and east of a further mapped confluence. The source channel continues west beyond the selected tip. The tip is geographically accounted for, but it is not independently established as a natural river mouth, salar sink or hydrological endorheic terminus. No extension to a coast or different receiving basin is substituted for the actual selected ending.

correspondence.component_scope: Surface and managed-passage scope across the complete selection
correspondence.finding: The whole-corridor waterbody view maps Salar Mar Muerto across the selected northward interruption; its other visible northeastern polygon is outside the selected opening. No additional lake or reservoir passage is established in the inspected selected corridor. Blank portions of this layer do not prove absence of temporary water, salt crust or small impoundments. No managed passage is identified or assumed.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen headward opening south of Tingui, west of Simão Dias
correspondence.finding: The Simão Dias original identifies Rio Jacaré on a headward branch south of Tingui and west of Lagoa da Vaca. The selected initial northern arm and its eastward hook are not actually connected to that named branch in the inspected cartography. Regional proximity is insufficient to establish this selected opening. The remaining southern continuation of part 1 approaches the mapped Jacaré corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Jacaré through Conceição de Campinas and São Domingos to the Caiçá join
correspondence.finding: The municipal original follows the selected southeastward valley through Conceição de Campinas and São Domingos, then east across the southern Simão Dias area. Rio Jacaré and the separately arriving Rio Caiçá are labelled near the eastern municipal boundary; their joined continuation runs toward Boeiro. All selected internal part joins in this corridor are accounted for at ordinary map scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Jacaré approach west of Lagarto
correspondence.finding: The Riachão do Dantas original traces Rio Jacaré south from Boeiro past Serrinha and Santo Antônio, across the western tributary junction near Jacaré and toward Jiboia. The selected southward turn, short intermediate parts and eastward approach to the impounded reach correspond to that mapped drainage. Nearby western watercourses carry their own Piauí/Piauitinga labels; no universal upstream name transition is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Mapped reservoir and downstream managed passage near Lagarto
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the widened reservoir between Jiboia, Apertado de Pedra and Barragem, beside the road labelled Estrada da Barragem Dionísio Machado. The selected west-to-east course crosses the depicted reservoir and continues into the mapped eastern/southeastern surface channel. This establishes the impounded geographic passage; it does not assert an independent reservoir hydronym or present operations.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle course toward Boquim and Arauá
correspondence.finding: The Riachão do Dantas original follows the channel past Cocão and the western Piauí tributary connection, Fazenda Piauí, Oiteiros and the Boquim-side corridor. Its southeastern continuation corresponds to the selected course toward the area covered by the Estância original. The latter traces the named Piauí corridor past Boquim and the eastern side of Arauá to its turn east toward Estância. The overlapping maps account for the selected small parts and tributary joins without adding the separate northern Piauitinga approach at Estância.

correspondence.component_scope: Estância and upper estuarine widening
correspondence.finding: The Estância original shows the river arriving from the west, the separate Piauitinga approach from the north, and the joined Rio Piauí along the southern side of Estância. The selected route continues east, turns south and then southeast through the Porto Grande/Miranga setting into the widening, island-bearing estuarine channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected terminal in the Piauí estuary
correspondence.finding: The actual terminal falls within the broad mapped Piauí estuarine channel in the Santa Luzia do Itanhy–Pindoba/Ilha das Tartarugas setting. The same original shows the island-bearing river continuing farther south toward the coast. The selected terminal is therefore accounted for as an estuarine endpoint, not asserted to be the ocean entrance. Exact tidal banks, individual island sides and current tidal or flow conditions are not required or claimed.
